facts.claim: In 2027 Earth reaches perihelion, its closest point to the Sun, on 3 January at 02:33 UT (08:03 in Sri Lanka, UT+5:30).
facts.single_source_reason: USNO is the primary almanac; the Sri Lanka time is UT plus the fixed +5:30 offset

facts.claim: Earth is closest to the Sun in January and farthest in July.
facts.source_sentence: And, believe it or not, aphelion (when Earth is farthest from the Sun) occurs in July, and perihelion (when we are closest) occurs in January. | NWS: Earth is at its closest point distance wise to the Sun in January (called the Perihelion) and the furthest in July (the Aphelion).

facts.claim: At its closest Earth is about 147 million km from the Sun; at its farthest, about 152 million km.
facts.source_sentence: Perihelion (10^6 km) 147.095; Aphelion (10^6 km) 152.100 | Space Place: Earth's perihelion (point closest to Sun) = 91,400,000 miles from Sun; Earth's aphelion (point farthest from Sun) = 94,500,000 miles from Sun (= 147.1 and 152.1 million km)

facts.claim: The difference is about 5 million km, small relative to the whole distance.
facts.source_sentence: 152.100 - 147.095 = 5.0 (10^6 km) | Space Place: While that is a difference of over 3 million miles, relative to the entire distance, it isn't much.

facts.claim: Seasons are caused by the tilt of Earth's axis, not by how far Earth is from the Sun.
facts.source_sentence: The Short Answer: Earth's tilted axis causes the seasons. | NWS: The seasons have nothing to do with how far the Earth is from the Sun. | NASA: This tilt causes our yearly cycle of seasons.

facts.claim: Earth's axis is tilted about 23.4 degrees.
facts.source_sentence: Earth's axis of rotation is tilted 23.4 degrees with respect to the plane of Earth's orbit around the Sun. | NSSDC: Obliquity to orbit (deg) 23.44 | NWS: tilted on its axis by an average of 23.5 degrees

facts.claim: Sri Lanka lies just north of the equator, between about 6 and 10 degrees north, and is warm all year.
facts.source_sentence: DoM: Between 05⁰ 55'N - 09⁰ 51'N Latitude | Wikipedia: Its position between 5 and 10 north latitude endows the country with year-round warm weather, moderated by ocean winds and considerable moisture.

facts.claim: Sri Lanka has four climate seasons set by the monsoons: first inter-monsoon March-April, southwest monsoon May-September, second inter-monsoon October-November, northeast monsoon December-February.
facts.source_sentence: Four Seasons • First Intermonsoon Mar - Apr • Southwest (summer) Monsoon May - Sep • Second Intermonsoon Oct - Nov • Northeast (winter) Monsoon Dec - Feb
facts.single_source_reason: the exact month ranges come only from the Department of Meteorology presentation (Dayananda 2010); meteo.gov.lk was unreachable; Wikipedia independently supports four monsoon-defined seasons with slightly different edges
facts.note: Wikipedia gives slightly different edges (SW mid-May to Oct, NE Dec to Mar); the Department of Meteorology's ranges are used.

facts.claim: Sri Lanka's temperature changes only a little through the year: in Colombo the average of the coolest month, January, is only about 2 °C below the warmest month.
facts.source_sentence: In Colombo, the average temperature of the coldest month (January) is of 27.4 °C, that of the warmest month (May) is of 29.2 °C. | Wikipedia: January is the coolest month
facts.single_source_reason: the 27.4/29.2 °C normals (1991-2020) come from one secondary site; the official normals (meteo.gov.lk) and the World Bank portal were unreachable. Wikipedia independently supports January as the coolest month. On screen only 'about 2 degrees' is used.
facts.note: Wikipedia's sentence copies the c.1988 Library of Congress country study; WorldClim 1970-2000 names December coolest. Say 'about 2 degrees' and avoid naming the warmest month on screen.

facts.claim: Averaged over the globe, sunlight reaching Earth in January is about 7% more intense than in July, but the tilt matters far more for the seasons.
facts.source_sentence: Averaged over the globe, sunlight falling on Earth in January is about 7% more intense than it is in July. | NSSDC: (152.100/147.095)^2 = 1.069
facts.single_source_reason: StarChild states the 7%; the second support is inverse-square arithmetic on the NSSDC perihelion and aphelion distances (1.069), not a second statement
